invariant: Java preserves source identity for parallel same-endpoint transitions across layout and painting. CucaDiagramFileMakerSvek groups links with the same connections without changing their relative source order, GraphvizImageBuilder constructs SvekEdge values in that order, and Bibliotekon retains those values in insertion order. SvekEdge.appendLine emits each relationship with a unique marker color, and SvekEdge.solveLine recovers the spline belonging to that original link by the marker rather than by endpoint geometry or Graphviz traversal order. Rust's LayoutGraph already preserves the equivalent identity: add_edge returns an insertion index, edge_specs associates that index with the returned Agedge_t pointer, and EdgePath exposes it after layout. Every later consumer must use the transition_index-to-layout-edge-index map. Parallel route identity is therefore neither endpoint-pair order, nearest endpoint distance, nor left-to-right lane order; it is the exact source transition attached to the routed edge instance.
causal_divergence: The flat state path records flat_transition_layout_edges while creating every transition and already uses that map when collecting the painted envelope. Final SVG emission discards it. routed_edge_path_for_transition scans every unconsumed spline and chooses the smallest sum of distances to the requested endpoint borders, while routed_self_edge_path chooses a geometric nesting order. Same-endpoint parallel transitions have the same endpoint score, so traversal order and tiny lane geometry decide which source label, path id, and arrowhead receive each spline. This is why the complete set of node positions, canvas dimensions, and route geometries match while only route ownership is exchanged. Direct experiments changing cgraph edge names, prebinding its attribute schema, node names, colors, and fixed-size flags left the heldouts unchanged, falsifying both preceding graph-construction hypotheses. Sorting paths, reversing declaration order, or assigning by label width would repeat the same identity loss in another form.
planned_change: Use flat_transition_layout_edges to resolve the exact EdgePath by edge_index in final flat-state transition emission, self links included. Use the same lookup for legacy label-bound calculations that currently consume paths by endpoint pair, so painting and sizing cannot disagree about ownership. Retain the endpoint-distance helpers only for rendering paths that genuinely lack caller identity outside this flat map. Verify the existing two-link pseudostate mesh, a renamed two-link graph with label widths exchanged, a fresh three-link same-endpoint graph with reordered declarations, and existing start/end and self-loop controls. Run focused renderer tests, the full no-oracle ratchet, and independent adversarial review. Do not sort routes geometrically, reverse parallel links, branch on edge count, inspect fixture labels, or derive identity from label dimensions.
